name: Isolated Neonatal Sclerosing Cholangitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Neonatal Sclerosing Cholangitis

criteria.description: Persistent neonatal cholestasis with conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
Histopathological evidence of sclerosing cholangitis with bile duct fibrosis and strictures
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the DCDC2 gene
Exclusion of other causes of neonatal cholestasis including biliary atresia and infectious etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent neonatal cholestasis, histopathological confirmation of sclerosing cholangitis, and pathogenic DCDC2 mutation with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver biopsy and genetic testing are critical for definitive diagnosis.

laboratory: Prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency
imaging: Cholangiography showing multifocal bile duct strictures and irregularities
Ultrasound revealing hepatomegaly without biliary atresia
other: Liver biopsy demonstrating periductal fibrosis, bile duct proliferation, and inflammatory infiltrates consistent with sclerosing cholangitis

distinguishingFeatures: Absence or obliteration of extrahepatic bile ducts
Early onset jaundice with pale stools
Severe liver failure with iron overload
Positive iron staining on liver biopsy

redFlags: Rapid progression to liver failure within first year of life
Failure to thrive despite nutritional support
Development of portal hypertension or cirrhosis in infancy
